- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, aggressively lower forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or adjust downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), reduce forecast slope and shift toward historical mean or 7-day moving average.  
- If forecast is >85 and true outcome drops below 75 within 5 days, apply downward correction of 5–10% for next 7 days unless sentiment reverts to positive.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 5 days show strong upward trend but true outcome diverges sharply (e.g., >10% deviation), reduce forecast by 2–5% for days 6–10 to avoid early overcommitment.  
- If sentiment history includes 1–2 positive spikes followed by negative values, model tends to overcorrect — apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast from day 3 onward.
